question: How much of each salt was dissolved per litre to make the three forward osmosis draw solutions, and to what osmotic pressure?
expect: NaCl 35.0 g/L, MgSO4.7H2O 71.8 g/L, sodium acetate 79.4 g/L, each to 30 bar at 25 C (sec. 2.2)
rendered:
<document title="A Comparative Study of Forward Osmosis Systems: An Integrated Experimental, Modeling, and Techno-Economic Analysis">

=== page 2 ===
- Deionized water (DI), characterized by a conductivity below 2 μS cm^− 1, and real municipal wastewater (WW), with a chemical oxygen demand (COD) of 460 mg L^− 1 and an osmotic pressure of 2.5 bar were employed as feed solutions.
- Draw solutions were prepared to provide an initial nominal osmotic pressure of 30 bar at 25 °C, using analytical-grade salts: NaCl (35.0 g L^−1), MgSO4·7H2O (71.8 g L^−1), and sodium acetate (79.4 g L^−1).
- Equal initial osmotic pressure (30 bar for all three draw solutions) was chosen to isolate draw solute chemistry as the variable under study, removing osmotic driving force as a confounding factor and giving each solution the same thermodynamic starting point.

The answer is:
- NaCl: 35.0 g/L
- MgSO4·7H2O: 71.8 g/L
- Sodium acetate: 79.4 g/L
- Osmotic pressure: 30 bar
